description: Signature original: Findings are grouped under the subquestions that produced them, in the mission's dependency order. title: Citation insertion from evidence links (foundational)
description: Signature original: Every factual sentence in the draft gets its citation inserted from the evidence links recorded during the investigation. Sentences with no link are flagged for the auditor instead of being published uncited. Citation insertion is mechanical and complete: no claim the evidence supports goes without its marker. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
links = {'inverted index hits 40ms': '[JAH-AT92-000003]'}
sent = 'inverted index hits 40ms'
print(sent, links.get(sent, '[NO CITATION -> flag]'))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Research Report Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Unresolved-question tracking (foundational)
description: Signature original: Subquestions that remain unanswered get their own report section with what was tried and why it fell short. Unresolved questions are first-class report content, not buried in a footnote, because they define the next investigation. Each one carries the negative-result summary from the analyzer. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
unresolved = [{'q': 'q3', 'tried': '12 queries across 2 collections', 'why': 'no primary sources found'}]
print('## Unresolved questions')
for u in unresolved: print(f" - {u['q']}: tried {u['tried']} ({u['why']})")
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Research Report Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Evidence summarization per section (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each report section opens with a two-sentence evidence summary: what was found and how strong the support is. Summaries are extractive, built from the top-scoring evidence passages, so they never drift from the sources. The summary lets busy readers get the point without reading every citation. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
evidence = ['inverted index: 40ms (strong)', 'scan: 900ms (strong)']
print('Evidence summary:', '; '.join(evidence[:2]) + '.')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Research Report Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Report assembly and completeness check (foundational)
description: Signature original: Assembly stitches sections, citations, summaries, and unresolved questions into the final document, then runs a completeness check: every subquestion appears exactly once, every factual sentence has a citation, and the unresolved section is non-empty when gaps exist. A report that fails the check goes back for repair instead of shipping incomplete. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
report = {'sections': 4, 'cited_sentences': 18, 'uncited': 0, 'unresolved_listed': True}
ok = report['uncited'] == 0 and report['unresolved_listed']
print('report complete:', ok)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Research Report Builder, 2026-10-21.
